g.title: iomap
g.text: MrZ80 -- Z-80 I/O port map, and the register windows inside the MMU, front-panel and PSG devices

g.title: cluster_io
g.text: I/O space: 8-bit ports, decoded on cpuAddress with IORQ

g.title: g0
g.text: device 1 → chip A, device 2 → chip B

g.title: p70
g.text: time-of-day supplied by the MiSTer HPS

g.title: p82
g.text: DDS baud rate, optional RTS/CTS, IRQ

g.title: p90
g.text: same registers, backed by a mounted image

g.title: pC0
g.text: 4 x 32-bit snapshots: 1 ms x2, 1 us x2

g.title: mc
g.text: a read or write is a physical memory access at the pointer,
the CPU is forced to wait for it

g.title: mn
g.text: 4 x 16 KB logical frames → a 28-bit physical space
(256 MB in 16 KB pages). SDRAM fills pages 0-8191,
the 64 KB block RAM sits at page 8192 (0x08000000).
Writing a frame's low byte clears its high byte: write $B0-$B3
first, then $B4-$B7. Frame 0 defaults to block RAM, or to
SDRAM page 0 once a .BIN boot image has been loaded.

g.title: f1
g.text: map bits 9:8 for $A5 writes, and reads

g.title: fn
g.text: 8 profiles x 256 WS2812/SK6812 LEDs, 384 capture-chain bits.
A .FPP profile file and the OSD profile override can select the
active profile without the Z-80's knowledge.

g.title: g3
g.text: deselects that device: DATA writes are dropped and
reads return $FF, like a real AY with a bad latched nibble

g.title: gn
g.text: Both chips feed both mixers. The OSD "PSG Stereo" choice
(status[26:25]) picks Mono / ABC / ACB and rewrites only the
gains, keeping software's master volume, invert, bass and treble.
Device 2 is panned the same way as device 1.
